subject: botany_2
question_text: What will be the phenotypic ratio in the offspring obtained from the following crosses: (a) Aa × aa (b) AA × aa (c) Aa × Aa (d) Aa × AA?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.42, printed question 89. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Four ratios, half a mark each. Work each one on a two-second Punnett square in the margin rather than from memory.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Principles of Inheritance and Variation (Botany-II) · 2 marks

steps.label: Parts a and b
steps.margin_note: Both crosses with the offspring written out, then the ratio.
lines: (a) Aa × aa  gives  Aa and aa
steps.why: Part (a) is a test cross and part (b) is a cross of two pure lines, which is why one splits evenly and the other does not split at all.
common_mistakes: Giving 3:1 for (a). Aa × aa is a TEST CROSS and gives 1:1.
Giving 1:1 for (b). AA × aa gives ALL dominant offspring.
steps.memory_tip: A test cross halves; two pure parents give one kind.

steps.label: Parts c and d
steps.margin_note: Both crosses, both ratios, and keep genotype separate from phenotype.

lines.text: Both parents must carry a recessive allele

lines: (c) Aa × Aa  gives  1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa
(d) Aa × AA  gives  AA and Aa, all dominant
steps.why: A recessive offspring needs a recessive allele from BOTH parents, so only the cross where both parents carry one can produce it.
common_mistakes: Giving 3:1 for (d). Aa × AA gives ALL dominant, because AA has no recessive allele.
Giving 1:2:1 as the phenotypic ratio for (c). 1:2:1 is the GENOTYPIC ratio; the phenotypic ratio is 3:1.
steps.memory_tip: No recessive allele in one parent means no recessive offspring.
